meta.title: Skep — Multi-Device AI Coding Agents over Live Sessions
meta.description: Coordinate AI coding agents across devices with join-code sessions and a local TUI. Open source CLI (@skepagent/skep). Credentials stay on each machine.
hero.title: Connected by live sessions.
hero.lead: Run AI coding agents on your laptop, GPU rig, and always-on server. Skep opens your local agent CLI, links devices with a join-code session TUI, and never moves provider credentials between machines.

howItWorks.title: Three steps, no infrastructure.
howItWorks.sub: Start a session on one device, join from others with a code. Agents stay local.
howItWorks.step1.title: Install & launch
howItWorks.step1.detail: Install {0} from npm. Run bare {1} in any repo to open your local agent CLI (claude, codex or pi).
howItWorks.step2.title: Start a session
howItWorks.step2.detail: Run {0} on a workstation. It prints a join code. Peers on the same machine or across the network join with that code—no shared git event log required.
howItWorks.step3.title: Assign work live
howItWorks.step3.body: Agents work on their own devices.
howItWorks.step3.detail: Use the session TUI ({0}) to see peers and items. Each device runs its own agent with its own login. You review and merge.
hive.title: A hive for agents. You hold the merge.
hive.sub: A skep is a traditional basket beehive. Here, the hive is a shared way of working: agents run on your devices, coordinate through live sessions, and bring the result back to you.
hive.tagline: Independent devices. Shared coordination. Human control.
hive.step1.label: 01 · Human
hive.step1.title: You set the goal
hive.step1.body: Describe the task and approve the plan before execution.
hive.step2.label: 02 · Skep
hive.step2.title: Skep coordinates
hive.step2.body: Use the CLI and session TUI to guide work across peers.
hive.step3.label: 03 · Local agents
hive.step3.title: Agents work locally
hive.step3.body: Agents run in local worktrees. Each device keeps its own provider credentials.
hive.step4.label: 04 · Session handoff
hive.step4.title: Peers hand off through the session
hive.step4.body: Master and peers exchange plans, claims, and results over the encrypted session channel. Full transcripts stay on the device that ran the agent.
hive.step5.label: 05 · Human merge
hive.step5.title: You review and merge
hive.step5.body: Inspect the code, checks, and stacked pull requests. You decide what merges.
hive.caption: A conceptual workflow, not a network map. Devices join a session master; code and pull requests live in your code repository.
hive.note: Session summaries travel between peers. They do not replace code review.
architecture.title: A session master. Local agents everywhere.
architecture.sub: You drive {0}. One device runs the session master; peers join with a code. Each machine keeps its own provider credentials. There is no central session to run or trust.
architecture.point1.title: Deterministic code enforces the protocol.
architecture.point1.body: Models only produce content: plans, reviews and code. sessions validate, authorize, sequence, test, sign and publish.
architecture.point2.title: No inbound connectivity (D18).
architecture.point2.body: session devices never connect to each other. No mesh VPN or fixed IP is required.
architecture.point3.title: Human holds the gates.
architecture.point3.body: You create tasks, approve plans, revoke leases, decide escalations and merge.
architecture.point4.title: Single-agent fast path by default.
architecture.point4.body: Team mode with several items, peer review and stacked PRs only when the task needs it.
features.title: Built for agents that don't share a machine.
features.execution.title: Dual-mode execution
features.execution.body: Use bare {0} to open your local agent interactively. Use the {1} session for background plan, review, claim and execute slots across devices.
features.session.title: live session
features.session.body: Commits as event logs. Every task, plan, lease and delivery is an SSH-signed event, verified against each device's local {0}. Forged or unsigned commits become no-ops and raise an alarm.
features.credentials.title: D19 credential isolation
features.credentials.body: Zero secret sharing. Each device's agent CLI uses its own local login. Keys never touch git or the wire, not even as a hash or a label.
features.leases.title: Epoch-fenced leases
features.leases.body: A claim bumps the work item's epoch, and every downstream event and branch is fenced by it. A laptop that wakes from sleep after its lease was revoked can never deliver stale work.
features.cli.title: Native CLI tooling
features.cli.body: A pure Node.js + TypeScript CLI with four runtime dependencies: {0}, {1}, {2} and {3}. It starts fast and stays small.
security.title: Security by architecture, not policy.
security.d19.title: Decision D19
security.d19.quote: “Skep never transports, stores, syncs or brokers provider credentials, API keys or provider configurations between devices, in any form: not as plaintext, not as ciphertext, not as a hash, and not as a label.”
security.devicesLabel: Each device uses its own credentials
security.chain.title: SSH-signed event chain
security.chain.body: Every session commit is signed with an SSH key and checked against a trust root that each device installs locally. Fingerprints are compared out of band at {0}.
security.noSync.title: Strict no-credential sync
security.d19.body: Other agent tools sync config and keys across devices. Skep explicitly forbids it. Machine A uses its Claude login and machine B uses its Codex login, and Skep never reads or records either.
security.audit.title: Auditable history
security.audit.body: When an agent makes a mistake, {0} on the session shows exactly which device, key and event made each step. The genesis commit is human-signed.
security.control.title: No auto-merge, ever
security.control.body: Plan approval, lease revocation, escalation decisions and merges stay with you. In session mode the master gets a redacted summary, and the full transcript stays on the device that did the work.
